papers.title: Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.
papers.abstract: Sequence-to-function (S2F) deep learning models predict genome-wide functional profiles directly from DNA sequences and have significantly advanced our understanding of gene regulation. However, existing S2F models are fundamentally constrained by their initial training datasets, and no single model encompasses the full spectrum of cell types, clinical conditions, and cellular states, while training new models de novo is nontrivial. Here, we develop Kidzoi, a kidney cell-type-specific S2F model obtained by transfer learning from the pretrained model Borzoi using single-nucleus chromatin access
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Kidzoi is a kidney cell-type-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in a cell-type-specific manner within the kidney, addressing the limitation that no single pretrained model covers all cell types and conditions. This approach provides a practical way to adapt existing S2F models to new tissues without training from scratch.

papers.title: Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Recent research has uncovered an unprecedented cell death pathway induced by outer membrane vesicles derived from Bergeyella cardium variant (BCV). This process promotes the pathological fusion of lysosome-related organelles via the SLC9A9 protein, leading to the formation of large vacuoles and ultimately inducing a terminal vacuolar cell death termed floatptosis. However, the role of floatptosis-related genes (FRGs) in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains largely unexplored. In this study, we constructed a LUAD prognostic model based on FRGs to predict patient prognosis and further explored the
papers.summary: This study builds a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes linked to floatptosis, a newly described form of vacuolar cell death triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. By combining single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, the authors link floatptosis-related gene expression to patient survival and to features relevant to immunotherapy response. The work is exploratory and the clinical utility of the model remains to be validated.

papers.title: Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence contributes to tumor progression and shapes the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet its prognostic and biological significance in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify senescence-associated prognostic signals through pan-cancer screening and to develop an integrated risk stratification framework for BLCA that bridges molecular characterization with translational relevance.
papers.summary: This study identifies cellular senescence-associated gene signatures through pan-cancer screening and builds a prognostic risk model for bladder urothelial carcinoma that integrates multi-omics and pathological data. The model stratifies patients by risk and links senescence signals to tumor microenvironment features, offering a framework for molecular risk stratification in BLCA.

papers.title: PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.
papers.abstract: Computationally designed DNA sequence libraries are essential components of massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs), deep mutational scanning (DMS) experiments, and other multiplex assays of variant effect (MAVEs). They are also increasingly used in silico to analyze genomic AI models. Designing these libraries, however, remains tedious and error-prone due to the scarcity of purpose-built software.
papers.summary: PoolParty is a Python package that streamlines the design of DNA sequence libraries for multiplex assays such as MPRA, DMS, and MAVE, as well as for in silico analysis of genomic AI models. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software that makes library design tedious and error-prone, providing a reusable tool for the genomics community.

papers.title: Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.
papers.abstract: Bull fertility is a key parameter in the dairy cattle industry, with significant economic implications. DNA methylation is an epigenetic mark essential for fertility, and recent works have highlighted sperm DNA methylation as a promising source of biomarkers for male fertility, but no operational tool has been developed for predicting bull fertility based on DNA methylation. Here, we leveraged existing methylation data to evaluate the potential of DNA methylation for predicting bull fertility with machine learning models.
papers.summary: This study tested whether DNA methylation patterns in Holstein bull sperm can predict bull fertility using machine learning models. Using existing methylation data, the authors evaluated the predictive power of sperm methylome features for fertility outcomes. The work assesses the feasibility of developing an operational methylation-based biomarker tool for the dairy cattle industry.

papers.title: Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous non-coding risk variants for prostate and ovarian cancers, yet determining which are regulatorily active and which target genes they control remains challenging. We re-analysed a dinucleotide-barcode massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) of 208 bi-allelic prostate cancer risk single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in three prostate cancer cell lines under false-discovery-rate (FDR) control, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10 (30 at FDR < 0.05), including 9 shared by at least two cell lines. Benchmarking standard in
papers.summary: The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) covering 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs across three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs at FDR < 0.10. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and used the findings to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer transfer. The work provides an experimentally grounded reference for evaluating computational regulatory variant predictions.

papers.title: Ultra-sensitive Mapping of Cell-free DNA-derived Methylomes Reveals Brain-specific Epigenetic Alterations Implicated in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: DNA cytosine modifications play a crucial role in gene regulation that underlies the pathogenesis of complex diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD). Using LABS ( L inear A mplification-based B isulfite S equencing), an ultra-sensitive linear amplification-based low-input whole-genome methylation profiling method, we demonstrated the feasibility of detecting altered methylation features in serum-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) between a set of age- and sex-matched pathologically-defined participants with AD and non-AD controls, from the Rush Memory and Aging Project. These blood methylation ch
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors applied LABS, an ultra-sensitive linear amplification-based whole-genome bisulfite sequencing method, to profile methylation in serum cell-free DNA from age- and sex-matched pathologically confirmed Alzheimer's disease cases and non-AD controls. They detected altered methylation features in blood cfDNA, including brain-specific epigenetic signatures, suggesting cfDNA methylomes can capture AD-related changes non-invasively.

papers.title: Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.
papers.abstract: The identification of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) and their associated metabolic pathways is central to genome-guided natural product discovery. However, existing computational tools depend on fragmented workflows for data processing, annotation, and analysis, which require substantial manual intervention and lack seamless integration across heterogeneous platforms and tools. Here, we present, Agent_K, an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the end-to-end process from bacterial whole genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic pathway mapping and metabolite discovery as candidate ge
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the entire workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) identification, pathway mapping, and candidate metabolite discovery. It addresses the fragmentation of existing computational tools by integrating data processing, annotation, and analysis across heterogeneous platforms with minimal manual intervention. This enables more streamlined genome-guided natural product discovery.

papers.title: Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.
papers.abstract: Disease-relevant changes in RNA processing frequently evade detection because they are missing from transcript annotations. Here, we introduce Torino , a computational framework that learns patterns of RNA processing directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data by modeling how coverage varies across samples, in datasets spanning tissues, individuals and disease states. Torino adapts non-negative matrix factorization to decompose coverage into patterns that capture RNA processing events, and to quantify their usage across samples, without transcript annotations. Across seven vertebrate sp
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model how read coverage varies across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and links them to disease risk across tissues, individuals, and disease states.

papers.title: Streamline CNV - A Handy Nextflow Pipeline for Chromosomal Copy Number Variation Analysis.
papers.abstract: Aneuploidy, characterized by imbalanced chromosomal copy number variation (CNV), occurs in both normal somatic tissues and a wide range of diseases. Low pass whole genome sequencing (LP-WGS) to detect CNVs in cells and tissues has been widely used in all biological research. Existing informatics tools for detecting CNV often require computational expertise, often posing challenges for wet-lab biologists. To address this need, we developed Streamline CNV (SLCNV) - a user-friendly and flexible copy number analysis pipeline that allows researchers to perform many copy number-related analyses step
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SLCNV is a user-friendly Nextflow pipeline that streamlines chromosomal copy number variation analysis from low-pass whole genome sequencing data, addressing the need for accessible tools for wet-lab biologists. It automates many copy number-related analyses, reducing the computational expertise required to detect aneuploidy and CNVs in cells and tissues.

papers.title: Viscous mechanical cues encode metastatic behavior through cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling.
papers.abstract: Tumors evolve within mechanically heterogeneous microenvironments, yet how cancer cells decode complex viscoelastic cues remains unresolved. Here, using hydrogels with independently tunable elasticity (G') and viscosity (G″), we show that viscous mechanical conditioning functionally mimics elastic rigidity. Cancer cells primed on elastically soft, viscous substrates adopt stiffness-associated states, including increased intrinsic stiffness, nuclear YAP accumulation, and enhanced migration through microfluidic constrictions. Epigenomic and transcriptomic profiling, coupled with viscoelastic com
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study shows that the viscosity of a tumor's mechanical environment can mimic the effects of stiffness on cancer cells. Cells grown on soft but viscous substrates develop stiffness-like traits, including increased cell stiffness, nuclear YAP accumulation, and enhanced migration through narrow constrictions. Epigenomic and transcriptomic profiling link these changes to cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling, suggesting viscosity is a distinct mechanical cue driving metastatic behavior.

papers.title: Combining MAVEs and computational predictors improves variant classification across ancestries in hereditary cancer genes.
papers.abstract: Many commonly used computational tools for variant effect prediction exhibit ancestry-related bias because they are trained on clinical or population datasets that under-represent global diversity, leading to uneven and sometimes unfair variant classification across ancestries. Multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) and population-free variant effect predictors (VEPs) instead offer alternatives that are unbiased with respect to human ancestry, providing classification evidence that generalises across populations.
papers.summary: This paper shows that widely used computational variant effect predictors carry ancestry-related bias because their training data under-represent global populations, leading to uneven classification of hereditary cancer gene variants across ancestries. The authors demonstrate that combining multiplexed assays of variant effect (MAVEs) with population-free predictors yields classification evidence that generalizes across populations, improving fairness and accuracy in variant interpretation.

papers.title: Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional chromatin organization shapes gene regulation by partitioning the genome into transcriptionally active and inactive compartments, with implications for prostate carcinogenesis. We integrated Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical samples representing benign prostatic hyperplasia, primary prostate cancer (PC), and castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). Using a computational framework accounting for copy number variation and tumor purity, we characterized A/B chromatin compartment organization in aneuploid tumors. We identified recurrent shifts from inac
papers.summary: By integrating Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical prostate samples spanning benign, primary, and castration-resistant cancer, this study maps A/B chromatin compartment changes while correcting for copy number variation and tumor purity. It finds recurrent shifts from inactive (B) to active (A) compartments in prostate tumors that are linked to epigenetic reprogramming, suggesting 3D genome reorganization contributes to prostate carcinogenesis and progression.

papers.title: Catalytic DNA for Precision Diagnostics: DNAzyme-Based Approaches to Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism Detection.
papers.abstract: Single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) are the most abundant form of human genetic variation and serve as important biomarkers in disease risk assessment, therapeutic stratification, and precision medicine. Yet accurate detection of low-abundance SNPs in complex biological samples remains difficult with many conventional genotyping methods, which often rely on sophisticated instrumentation and show limited tolerance to matrix interference. DNAzyme-based biosensors offer a promising alternative by coupling programmable nucleic acid recognition with catalytic signal generation under isothermal c
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
papers.summary: This review examines DNAzyme-based biosensors for detecting single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), the most common form of human genetic variation and key biomarkers for disease risk and precision medicine. It argues that these catalytic DNA sensors overcome limitations of conventional genotyping methods—such as reliance on sophisticated instruments and poor tolerance of complex sample matrices—by combining programmable nucleic acid recognition with isothermal catalytic signal amplification.

papers.title: Ultrafast alignment-free detection of viral genome variation with bronko.
papers.abstract: As viral sequencing datasets continue to grow, traditional alignment-based variant calling pipelines are becoming computationally prohibitive. To address these challenges, we developed bronko, an ultrafast alignment-free framework for detecting viral variation directly from sequencing data. The novel computational approach implemented in bronko allows scaling to massive viral sequencing datasets and has four key components: i) a locality-sensitive bucketing function to rapidly identify single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) relative to reference(s), ii) a direct k-mer count pseudo-mapping appr
papers.summary: The authors present bronko, an alignment-free framework that detects viral genome variation directly from sequencing reads, avoiding the computational cost of traditional alignment-based variant calling. It uses locality-sensitive bucketing to rapidly identify SNPs relative to a reference and a k-mer count pseudo-mapping approach, enabling scaling to massive viral sequencing datasets.

papers.title: O-acetylation mediates four distinct structural variants of the pneumococcal vaccine serotype 15A capsule polysaccharide.
papers.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae vaccine efforts rely on serological or molecular typing schemes to categorize over 100 biochemically distinct capsule polysaccharides (cPS) produced by the pathobiont; however, conventional approaches can fail to capture variations in key cPS biochemical features, such O-acetylation (OAc) patterns. The non-acetylated serotype 15A cPS is included in newer pneumococcal conjugate vaccine formulations and has one characterized acetylated counterpart, 15F. Report of a potential second variant "15D" prompted re-investigation of serogroup 15 capsule types.
papers.summary: This study re-examined the capsule polysaccharides of pneumococcal serogroup 15 and found that O-acetylation generates four distinct structural variants of the 15A capsule, not just the previously recognized 15A and 15F forms. The findings show that conventional serological and molecular typing can miss O-acetylation differences that may affect vaccine coverage and serotype classification.

papers.title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for livestock genetics and breeding.
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming modern society including animal genetics and breeding which is essential for meeting global nutritional needs in supplying milk, meat, and eggs among the most complete sources of protein and micronutrients. Although animal breeding has a long history of using data-driven prediction methods, the application of modern AI approaches remains at a relatively early stage and shows substantial potential for wide-ranging applications in animal genetics and breeding. This study aims to review the current use of AI tools in livestock
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence tools are currently applied to livestock genetics and breeding, noting that while animal breeding has long relied on data-driven prediction, modern AI methods are still at an early stage of adoption. The authors highlight substantial untapped potential for AI to improve selection, prediction, and breeding decisions for milk, meat, and egg production.

papers.title: Integrated optimization of experimental and computational workflows improves genome recovery in long-read gut metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Short-read metagenomic sequencing has been widely applied in microbial research due to its high quality and decreasing cost. However, short reads are inherently fragmented, which limits assembly contiguity and the recovery of complete microbial genomes. In contrast, long-read sequencing, with significantly longer read lengths, helps overcome these limitations. Achieving complete and accurate genome recovery is the core goal of metagenomics. To address this challenge, we systematically evaluated and optimized the long-read metagenomic workflow, from sample processing to computational assembly,
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates and optimizes a long-read metagenomic workflow, from sample processing through computational assembly, to improve recovery of complete microbial genomes from gut microbiome samples. By integrating experimental and computational optimizations, the authors show that long-read sequencing can overcome the fragmentation limits of short-read approaches and yield more contiguous, complete genomes.

papers.title: Proteomics-Guided Discovery of Candidate Enzymes for Degradation of a Rare Pyruvylated Glycosaminogalactan by a Newly Isolated Luteolibacter Strain.
papers.abstract: Bacterial exopolysaccharides (EPS) display extensive structural diversity arising from variation in monosaccharide composition, glycosidic linkages, and non-carbohydrate modifications. However, the enzymes responsible for degrading many EPS structures remain unknown, reflecting the limited coverage of current carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) families. Here, we investigated the microbial degradation of EPSLp, a high-molecular-mass glycosaminogalactan from Lactiplantibacillus pentosus KW1 containing the uncommon GalNAcβ1 → 2(4,6-O-R-pyruvyl)Gal motif. Enrichment cultivation with EPSLp as the
papers.summary: The authors isolated a new Luteolibacter strain capable of degrading EPSLp, a high-molecular-mass exopolysaccharide from Lactiplantibacillus pentosus that contains an uncommon pyruvylated GalNAc-Gal motif. Using proteomics to identify proteins induced during growth on EPSLp, they nominated candidate carbohydrate-active enzymes responsible for its degradation. This work expands knowledge of the enzymatic machinery for degrading structurally unusual bacterial EPS.

papers.title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic ta
papers.summary: This study combines bioinformatics analysis of public HCC transcriptomic datasets with in vitro experiments to show that sodium propionate, a short-chain fatty acid, exerts anticancer effects on hepatocellular carcinoma cells by downregulating the histone deacetylases HDAC2 and HDAC6. The work identifies these HDACs as key epigenetic targets through which sodium propionate may act, suggesting a potential repurposing opportunity for this metabolite in liver cancer.

papers.title: Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.
papers.abstract: Caenorhabditis nematodes represent a promising model clade for evolutionary genetics and genomics, but research has focused on the three androdioecious species, those with self-fertile hermaphrodites, all in the Elegans Group of species. The majority of Caenorhabditis species are gonochorists, with males and females, characterized by inconveniently high heterozygosity and inbreeding depression. We have identified C. becei as an experimentally tractable gonochorist. We show that transmission-genetic properties known from the androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Gr
papers.summary: The authors identify Caenorhabditis becei as an experimentally tractable gonochoristic (male-female) nematode species, addressing the field's reliance on self-fertile hermaphroditic Elegans Group species. They show that transmission-genetic properties known from androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Group species, making it a useful new model for evolutionary genetics and genomics.

papers.title: CALB1 expression in meningioma: associations with progression-free survival and chromosome arm 6q loss.
papers.abstract: Molecular profiling has refined risk stratification in meningioma, but the biological relevance of associated transcriptional changes remains incompletely understood. Calbindin D28K (Calb), encoded by CALB1, is a calcium-binding protein with reported anti-apoptotic and cytoprotective functions. Previous unsupervised transcriptomic analysis identified CALB1 upregulation in meningiomas with aggressive cellular features, but its biological and clinical relevance remains unresolved. We analysed Calb immunoreactivity in 231 meningioma tissue microarray (TMA) cores from 147 patients and evaluated CA
papers.summary: This study examined calbindin D28K (CALB1) protein expression in 231 meningioma tissue cores from 147 patients and found associations between CALB1 immunoreactivity, progression-free survival, and chromosome arm 6q loss. The work links a transcriptional marker of aggressive meningioma biology to clinical outcomes and a specific genomic alteration, helping clarify the biological relevance of CALB1 upregulation.

papers.title: Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.
papers.abstract: Plant breeding is entering a multimodal era in which genomic, phenotypic, environmental, and multi-omics data are generated alongside a rapidly expanding scientific literature. Text-based large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models (Bio-FMs) offer complementary capabilities for organizing evidence, representing biological relationships, and learning from molecular data. Here, we review these technologies across knowledge mining, predictive modeling, and intelligent breeding design, and apply a systematic evidence audit to dis
papers.summary: This review examines how large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, knowledge graphs, and biological foundation models can support predictive plant breeding by integrating genomic, phenotypic, environmental, and multi-omics data with scientific literature. It surveys applications across knowledge mining, predictive modeling, and breeding design, and includes a systematic evidence audit highlighting gaps between claimed capabilities and demonstrated results.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a heterogeneous disease that results from the progressive accumulation and interactions at multiple levels of genetic alterations, which lead to the transformation of normal colonic epithelium into malignant colorectal tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of CRC pathogenesis, together with the interactions between genetic alterations, epigenetic modifications, environmental and lifestyle factors, is essential for improving prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies. This review aims to provide a critical reference point for understanding the temp
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms driving colorectal cancer, from the stepwise accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations that transform normal colonic epithelium into malignancy, through molecular classification systems, to the implications for targeted therapy. It emphasizes how interactions among genetic changes, epigenetic modifications, and environmental/lifestyle factors shape prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment. The work serves as a consolidated reference for understanding the molecular landscape of CRC.

papers.title: Lysine crotonylation acts as an epigenetic switch for glutamate neurotransmission and spatial memory.
papers.abstract: Histone posttranslational modifications, particularly lysine acetylation (Kac), are critical epigenetic regulators of transcriptional programs underlying long-term memory consolidation. Beyond Kac, several other non-acetyl acylations have been identified with the ability to regulate transcription; however, their role in memory consolidation remains unknown. Here, we identify histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a molecular switch for long-term memory and glutamatergic neurotransmission. We find that spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study identifies histone lysine crotonylation (Kcr) as a key epigenetic regulator of long-term memory consolidation. Spatial learning induces distinct spatiotemporal patterns of Kcr across hippocampal subregions, and Kcr appears to act as a molecular switch controlling glutamatergic neurotransmission and spatial memory. The work extends the known epigenetic repertoire beyond histone acetylation in memory formation.

papers.title: A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection.
papers.abstract: Accurate detection of Z-DNA-forming regions is limited by the trade-off between sensitivity and specificity in sequence-based methods. We present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0-a fast and interpretable protocol that extends Z-DNA Hunter through a dual-scan strategy combined with a fuzzy expert layer. A permissive scan (model 2, minimum length 6 bp, threshold 30%) captures a broad candidate set, while a stringent scan (model 2, minimum length 10 bp, threshold 60%) provides high-confidence support. These outputs are integrated using fuzzy inference incorporating sequence signal, cross-scan support, ge
papers.summary: The authors present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0, a tool that improves detection of Z-DNA-forming regions by combining a permissive scan (broad candidate capture) with a stringent scan (high-confidence support) and integrating them through a fuzzy expert layer. This dual-scan recall-rescue strategy aims to overcome the sensitivity-specificity trade-off in sequence-based Z-DNA prediction while remaining fast and interpretable.

papers.title: Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.
papers.abstract: Causal structure inference under the principle of Mendelian randomization (PMR) enables the study of causal relationships between two molecular phenotypes (e.g. gene expression) by leveraging genetic variants as instrumental variables to impose constraints on edge direction. In practice, inference is often affected by numerous confounding variables, such as other genes, other processes and demographic variables, making it essential to robustly account for confounders. However, existing methods have limited ability to accommodate high-dimensional confounding. Here, we introduce Mendelian random
papers.summary: The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (like gene expression) using genetic variants as instruments under the Mendelian randomization principle, specifically designed to handle high-dimensional confounding variables such as other genes, processes, and demographics. Existing methods struggle with such high-dimensional confounders, and this work aims to robustly account for them in causal network inference for genomic trio data.

papers.title: XenoMix: estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation microarrays enable cost-effective, high-throughput profiling of human and mouse samples and are widely used to study epigenetic alterations in cancer. Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models complement this approach by preserving primary tumor characteristics while enabling in vivo studies of drug response and therapy resistance. However, it remains difficult to quantify mouse DNA contamination in PDX DNA methylation data generated using microarrays. We present XenoMix, a light-weight computational tool for quantifying mouse DNA contamination directly from DNA methylation data i
papers.summary: XenoMix is a lightweight computational tool that estimates the proportion of mouse DNA contamination in DNA methylation microarray data from Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) models. It addresses the common problem of mixed human-mouse signal in PDX epigenomic profiling, enabling researchers to quantify and account for contamination without additional experiments. This improves the reliability of epigenetic analyses in PDX-based cancer studies.

papers.title: SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.
papers.abstract: Staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements are mobile genetic elements that integrate at the rlmH gene and are predominantly responsible for methicillin resistance in staphylococci. Although staphylococcal cassette chromosome mec (SCCmec) typing tools exist, none can extract the element sequence itself or explicitly classify SCC elements that lack methicillin resistance genes. Here, we present SCCmecExtractor, a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies SCC element boundaries through degenerate attachment site (att) pattern matching, extracts complete elements from whole-genome assembl
papers.summary: SCCmecExtractor is a new lightweight Python toolkit that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by detecting degenerate attachment site patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the full element sequence and classify SCC elements even when they lack methicillin resistance genes. This enables more comprehensive analysis of these mobile genetic elements in staphylococci.

papers.title: The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.
papers.abstract: Metabolic traits mediate microbial interactions and underpin mechanistic models of community assembly. With the rapid expansion of genomic data and bioinformatic tools, it is widely assumed that metabolic traits such as substrate utilization can be reliably inferred from genomes alone. Here, we systematically evaluate this assumption by comparing genome-based predictions from four commonly used tools to high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria. For simple substrates, prediction accuracy was limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, with many strains predicted at o
papers.summary: This study systematically tests whether metabolic traits like substrate utilization can be reliably predicted from bacterial genomes alone. Comparing four common bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria, the authors find that prediction accuracy is limited and highly variable across taxa and substrates, especially for simple substrates. The results caution against assuming that genome-based metabolic predictions are universally reliable.

papers.title: Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.
papers.abstract: Loss-of-function (LOF) variants of the FLG gene are risk factors for atopic dermatitis. However, owing to the repetitive nature of exon 3, these variants are difficult to characterize. We sought to determine whether the use of long-read technologies would enable better characterization of the FLG gene and improve the detection of LOF variants. We sequenced a diverse clinical cohort of 192 samples collected in Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda using long-read sequencing as well as publicly available data. We identified both common and rare LOF variants linked to atopic dermatitis in our clinical coh
papers.journal: JID innovations : skin science from molecules to population health
papers.summary: Using long-read sequencing on 192 samples from Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda, researchers characterized the repetitive exon 3 of the FLG gene, revealing extensive copy number variation and identifying both common and rare loss-of-function variants associated with atopic dermatitis. Long-read technology overcame the limitations of short-read methods in this repetitive region, improving detection of clinically relevant LOF variants.

papers.title: MLMP: A Methylation-Associated lncRNA-mRNA Prognostic Signature for Endometrial Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is one of the most common gynecological malignancies. Aberrant DNA methylation (DNAm) is an important epigenetic alteration involved in cancer progression. Long non-coding RNAs (LncRNAs) play critical roles in gene regulation and pathological processes. However, the biological and prognostic significance of lncRNA-mRNA pairs associated with methylation remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study develops MLMP, a prognostic signature for endometrial carcinoma built from methylation-associated lncRNA-mRNA pairs, aiming to link DNA methylation, lncRNA regulation, and patient outcome. It identifies methylation-driven lncRNA-mRNA interactions with prognostic value, offering a multi-omic biomarker framework for risk stratification in EC. The work extends existing prognostic modeling approaches by incorporating epigenetic regulation of non-coding RNA networks.

papers.title: Epigenetic Insights in Pediatric Multiple Sclerosis: DNA Methylation Highlights an Involvement of Epstein-Barr Virus Infection and Host Immune Networks.
papers.abstract: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS) provides a unique opportunity to investigate MS pathogenesis because of the short interval between environmental exposures and disease onset. This study aimed to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) that mediate the interplay between environmental triggers and genomic factors in the early stages of the disease.
papers.summary: This study profiled DNA methylation in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (PedMS), a form of MS with a short interval between environmental exposure and disease onset, to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs). The findings point to Epstein-Barr virus infection and host immune networks as key players, suggesting that EBV-related epigenetic changes may contribute to early MS pathogenesis.

papers.title: MethyAnno: An Interpretable Automated Annotation Method Leveraging Multi-Scale Information and Metric Learning Framework for scDNAm Data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) sequencing provides unique insights into epigenetic heterogeneity and cell-specific regulatory landscapes. However, accurate cell type annotation for scDNAm data remains challenging, as the distinct data distribution of scDNAm hinders the adaptation of annotation methods from other omics, and specialized annotation tools for scDNAm are currently lacking. Here, MethyAnno is proposed as an interpretable deep metric learning framework that leverages multi-scale information for accurate cell type annotation of scDNAm data. Additionally, MethyAnno enables genera
papers.summary: MethyAnno is a new interpretable deep metric learning framework that annotates cell types in single-cell DNA methylation (scDNAm) data by leveraging multi-scale information. It addresses the lack of specialized annotation tools for scDNAm, whose distinct data distribution prevents direct adaptation of methods from other omics. The method enables accurate, interpretable cell type annotation and broader downstream analyses for scDNAm studies.

papers.title: Ultra-deep HiFi sequencing reveals rare structural-variant subpopulations in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa from an LVAD-associated infection.
papers.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a Gram-negative opportunistic pathogen frequently associated with multidrug-resistant infections in clinical settings. The rise of antibiotic-resistant strains and their genomic complexity necessitate advanced tools for comprehensive genetic characterization, particularly in the context of resistance to antibiotic and phage therapies.
papers.summary: This study applies ultra-deep HiFi long-read sequencing to a multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate from a left ventricular assist device (LVAD)-associated infection, uncovering rare structural-variant subpopulations within the bacterial population. The work demonstrates that deep long-read sequencing can resolve within-host genomic heterogeneity that standard approaches miss, with implications for understanding resistance to both antibiotics and phage therapy.

papers.title: cgMLST typing reproducibility is maintained across diverse whole-genome sequencing workflows in a multi-country HERA2 surveillance pilot.
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) has become indispensable in infectious disease surveillance, yet its implementation across laboratories remains heterogeneous. Six laboratories from four European countries participated in 2023 in a pilot ring trial as part of the HERA2 project, using a standardized panel of 25 bacterial isolates representing five public health-relevant species. The aim was to assess the comparability and reproducibility of laboratory-specific WGS workflows and to determine whether workflow-related variability affected cgMLST-based interpretations relevant for routine surveillance
papers.summary: This multi-country ring trial tested whether different laboratories' whole-genome sequencing workflows produce comparable core-genome MLST (cgMLST) typing results for bacterial surveillance. Six labs in four European countries sequenced a standardized panel of 25 isolates from five public health-relevant species, and cgMLST-based interpretations remained reproducible across the diverse workflows. The findings support the robustness of cgMLST typing for routine cross-laboratory surveillance despite heterogeneous sequencing implementation.

papers.title: Survey of viruses associated with the whitefly Bemisia tabaci in cucurbits in Georgia, United States.
papers.abstract: Whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) are major agricultural pests causing over $100 million in losses to vegetable production annually through the transmission of plant viruses. Characterizing the virome of B. tabaci is critical for understanding vectoring potential and identifying candidate viral biocontrol agents. In this study, B. tabaci were collected from cucurbit crops in Tifton, Georgia, across two consecutive years, 2023 and 2024. Total RNA was extracted and ribodepleted, then sequenced with 150 bp paired-end reads on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Bioinformatics analyses included quality-assessing
papers.summary: This study surveyed the virome of whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) collected from cucurbit crops in Georgia over two consecutive years using RNA sequencing. The work characterizes which viruses are associated with this major agricultural pest, which is important for understanding its potential to transmit plant viruses and for identifying candidate viral biocontrol agents.

papers.title: Genomic profiling and drug resistance patterns of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Indonesia: whole-genome sequencing of isolates from the 2017-2018 national Tuberculosis Drug Resistance Survey.
papers.abstract: Drug-resistant tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia. This study aimed to characterize the genetic diversity, lineage distribution, and genotypic resistance profiles of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates across the Indonesian archipelago using whole-genome sequencing.
papers.summary: This study used whole-genome sequencing to characterize Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates collected during Indonesia's 2017–2018 national drug resistance survey, mapping lineage distribution and genotypic resistance profiles across the archipelago. It provides a nationwide genomic snapshot of drug-resistant TB in Indonesia, linking genetic diversity to geographic spread and resistance patterns.

papers.title: Design and validation of nucleosome binding peptides using BindCraft.
papers.abstract: Chromatin is a sophisticated assembly of DNA, RNA and proteins in the nuclei of eukaryotic cells. Protein-protein interactions that govern chromatin function are key regulators of genome activity, making them prime targets for drug discovery. Engineering and modulating these contacts presents a viable pathway for innovative epigenetic therapies. Nucleosomes, the primary structural units of chromatin, feature various interaction interfaces, most notably the acidic patch. This region serves as a critical binding site for numerous chromatin-associated proteins, often via their intrinsically disor
papers.summary: The authors used the BindCraft computational protein design tool to engineer peptides that bind the nucleosome acidic patch, a key chromatin interaction interface. They then experimentally validated the designed peptides, demonstrating that computational design can produce functional chromatin-binding molecules. This work supports using de novo design to create tools or leads for epigenetic therapies targeting chromatin protein-protein interactions.

papers.title: Assembly and comparative analysis of the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii Maxim. (Cannabaceae), a tertiary relict plant endemic to China.
papers.abstract: Pteroceltis tatarinowii Maxim. (Cannabaceae) is a deciduous arbor endemic to China. As a Tertiary relict plant, it is listed as a rare and endangered species under national Class III key protection. Mitochondrial genomic data of P. tatarinowii can improve our knowledge of phylogenetic relationships within Cannabaceae, resolve the taxonomic placement and evolutionary divergence of the genus Pteroceltis, and supply molecular support for conservation and genetic breeding of this endangered tree.
papers.summary: This study assembled and analyzed the mitochondrial genome of Pteroceltis tatarinowii, a rare Tertiary relict tree endemic to China. The mitochondrial genomic data were used to clarify phylogenetic relationships within Cannabaceae and the evolutionary placement of the genus Pteroceltis, providing molecular support for conservation and breeding of this endangered species.

papers.title: ogMapper improves speed and memory for short-sequencing read mapping using a novel guided sparse genome index.
papers.abstract: Short DNA-read sequencing has become an everyday essential tool in research and clinical setting. Read mapping is a crucial step that consumes large amounts of memory and CPU time, limiting the hardware required and ultimately restricting its applications. The memory required for the genome index can be approximated as βG, where G is the genome size and β is a factor that depends on the implementation. For example, β ≈ 10 for bwa-mem2 or β ≈ 1.9 for minimap2. Here, an indexing strategy is presented in which β can be even less than 1, commonly around 0.5. The indexing strategy relies on "guides
papers.summary: ogMapper introduces a novel guided sparse genome indexing strategy for short-read mapping that reduces the memory footprint of the genome index to roughly 0.5 times the genome size (β ≈ 0.5), compared to β ≈ 1.9 for minimap2 and β ≈ 10 for bwa-mem2. This lower memory requirement, combined with improved speed, makes read mapping feasible on less powerful hardware, broadening its applicability in research and clinical settings.

papers.title: vardictcpp: a C++ reimplementation of VarDict variant caller.
papers.abstract: Genomic variant calling is a central computational task in disease research and diagnostics, where somatic mutations such as JAK2 V617F serve as diagnostic markers in myeloid neoplasms. VarDict, originally written in Perl, and its reimplementation VarDictJava are widely used variant callers in the bioinformatics community. The Perl implementation requires run times of up to several hours; VarDictJava reduces this to a few minutes but can consume large amounts of main memory, which limits the number of jobs that can be run in parallel on a given machine. We present vardictcpp, a functionally id
papers.summary: vardictcpp is a C++ reimplementation of the widely used VarDict variant caller, designed to overcome the slow runtime of the original Perl version and the high memory usage of VarDictJava. It aims to provide equivalent variant calling functionality with improved computational efficiency, enabling more parallel jobs on a given machine.

papers.title: Discriminating malignancy of pulmonary nodules using a peripheral blood leukocyte DNA methylation-based SEMO network model.
papers.abstract: Accurately discriminating malignant pulmonary nodules from benign lesions remains challenging, particularly in subcentimeter lesions. This study developed and internally validated a peripheral blood leukocyte (PBL) DNA methylation-derived Selective Epigenomic Module Optimization (SEMO) network model to improve risk stratification.
papers.summary: This study developed a blood-based DNA methylation model, called SEMO, that uses peripheral blood leukocytes to distinguish malignant pulmonary nodules from benign ones, with a focus on hard-to-classify subcentimeter lesions. The model was built and internally validated, suggesting that epigenomic network features from routine blood samples could aid lung cancer risk stratification.

papers.title: AI and computational methods for reconstructing cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptome and chromatin accessibility data in cancer: methods, applications, and perspectives.
papers.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity is shaped by genetic, epigenetic, microenvironmental, and stochastic factors, among which cell-state-specific regulatory programs are a major determinant. Gene regulatory networks provide a systems-level model linking transcription factors, cis-regulatory elements, and target genes. Paired single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) measure chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cell, offering a direct view of regulatory elements and transcriptional output; matched-but-unpai
papers.summary: This review surveys AI and computational methods for reconstructing cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks by integrating single-cell RNA-seq and scATAC-seq data, with a focus on cancer heterogeneity. It covers paired and unpaired integration strategies, network inference approaches, and applications in understanding tumor regulatory programs, while outlining remaining challenges and future directions.

papers.title: Tissue-specific moderate DNA methylation alterations featuring hypomethylation in microRNA regulatory regions associated with advanced carotid atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation is an important epigenetic mechanism involved in the regulation of gene expression, but its contribution to the regulation of microRNA genes in atherosclerosis remains poorly understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study examines DNA methylation changes in carotid atherosclerotic plaques, focusing on microRNA regulatory regions. It finds moderate, tissue-specific hypomethylation at microRNA regulatory regions associated with advanced atherosclerosis, suggesting epigenetic dysregulation of microRNA genes may contribute to disease progression.
